english.title: Fell a growing tree without a section 9(1) felling licence - England
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), on an area of woodland felled growing timber without the authority of a licence issued by the appropriate forestry authority under section 9(1) of the Forestry Act 1967
english.legislation: Contrary to section 17(1) of the Forestry Act 1967.

english.notes:
(i) The penalty for this offence changed for offences committed in England on or after 1st January 2023; for offences committed before that date in England or Wales see H7991, for offences committed in Wales from 1st January 2023, see H101125.
(ii) Section 9(2) of the Forestry Act 1967 provides that the requirement for a felling licence does not apply -
(a) to the felling of trees with a diameter not exceeding 8 centimetres or, in the case of coppice or underwood, with a diameter not exceeding 15 centimetres; or
(b) to the felling of fruit trees or trees standing or growing on land comprised in an orchard, garden, churchyard or public open space; or
(c) to the topping or lopping of trees or the trimming or laying of hedges.
(iii) See also section 9(3) to 9(6) of the Forestry Act 1967.
(iv) Section 17(2) of the Forestry Act 1967 provides that proceedings for an offence under this section may be instituted within six months from the first discovery of the offence by the person taking the proceedings, provided that no proceedings shall be instituted more than two years after the date of the offence.
